title: Satellite telemetry bridge for private cluster trunking and replayable buffering
creator: Amira Chen
description: Build a lightweight 'satellite bridge' daemon to run inside customer VPCs / on-prem clusters that (1) securely trunks traces/metrics/logs to Redwood ingest, (2) provides tenant-aware buffering and replay for transient network partitions, and (3) exposes standardized tracing hooks so application teams can opt into low-latency sampling paths. This ticket covers design, PoC, and initial integration tests for the bridge and replay flow.
acceptance_criteria: Bridge runs as a small footprint container (<=200MB) inside customer clusters
TLS-encrypted, KMS-signed envelopes for all outbound telemetry (OTLP over gRPC preferred) with per-tenant auth headers
Local replay store can persist up to 24 hours of compressed telemetry and restore to hosted ingest with ordered, idempotent delivery
No cross-tenant observability leakage under multi-tenant load (verified by integration tests)
End-to-end additional tail latency <= 200ms for sampled trace forwarding under steady state
Can flip to buffered-replay mode automatically on network degraded signal and drain to hosted ingestion once connectivity recovers
technical_decisions: Transport: OTLP/gRPC chosen for traces and logs because of built-in batching and flow-control; Prometheus remote_write will be used for metrics where customers expose scrape targets
Buffering: local disk-backed append-only LZ4-compressed segments with tombstones for ordered replay and efficient tail truncation
Replay semantics: exactly-once best-effort via per-record idempotency tokens + sequence watermarks; receiver acknowledges high-water marks to GC local segments
Security: per-tenant mTLS using short-lived certs from Redwood CA; outbound envelopes signed with customer-key-wrapped signing keys in KMS
Sampling hooks: lightweight HTTP endpoint (local) for SDKs to call for deterministic sampling decisions, with cached policies and RTT-aware fallback
Backpressure: implement adaptive batching with latency SLO control algorithm that trades batch size for tail latency using an EWMA latency estimator
Telemetry enrichment: translate local trace headers into Redwood canonical trace_id and append tenant_id and origin metadata before sending
design_notes: Bridge will expose a small admin HTTP port for health, metrics (Prometheus), and a secured replay API for customer-initiated replays
Operational modes: 'trunk' (pass-through with small buffer), 'buffering' (conserve memory/IO and persist segments), and 'replay' (drain to hosted ingest).
Disk layout: rotate segment files at 64MB with manifest file for active segments; use atomic rename for commit
Isolation: enforce per-tenant disk quotas and runtime cgroups to prevent noisy-neighbor IO/CPU impact
Observability: add internal metrics to monitor buffer occupancy, replay throughput, handshake latencies, and signature verification failures
prototype_notes: PoC built as go binary (satbridge) using otlpgrpc and boltdb for manifest; initial PoC in feature branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/satbridge/pull/74
PoC validated ordered replay of traces for one tenant across simulated partitions (network-delay/local-disk-full scenarios)
Disk-pressure tests show prioritization heuristic prevents OOMs but IO tail can exceed SLO on 1 vCPU nodes — need tuned IO scheduler or cgroup throttling

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Local disk IO could impact application nodes under heavy load. Mitigation: enforce cgroup IO weight and provide guidance for node sizing.
Risk: Certificate management complexity for short-lived per-tenant certs. Mitigation: automated rotation via Redwood control-plane signed CSR flow + local caching
Risk: Replay duplication due to network retries. Mitigation: idempotency tokens + server-side watermark ack + replay GC strategy
Risk: Regulatory/legal restriction on telemetry egress for air-gapped customers. Mitigation: support operator-driven export keys and offline media export; defer to Private deployment support plan
